findings.title: Use of subprocess.run with shell=True can enable command injection
findings.explanation: The code executes a fixed git command using subprocess.run with shell=True. While the current command string is static, using shell=True unnecessarily expands the attack surface and could become vulnerable if the command string is ever modified to include user input.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the shell invocation with a list argument and set shell=False, e.g., subprocess.run(["git", "rev-parse", "--short", "HEAD"], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).

findings.title: Avoid shell=True with string arguments in subprocess.run
findings.explanation: Using shell=True with a single string argument bypasses the typical subprocess interface and can lead to security and portability issues. The idiomatic way is to pass the command as a list of arguments and omit shell=True.
findings.suggested_fix:
Replace the call with
```python
commit = subprocess.check_output(["git", "rev-parse", "--short", "HEAD"], text=True).strip()
```
